_note: Corrections to app copy for website animal pages only (from naturalist/child-psych review). Each: {appId, find, replace}. Applied by _data/liteAnimals.js. Route the same fixes to the app via wild-atlas-i18n.

overrides.find: but they're about 100 times bigger!
overrides.replace: but they're about 50 times bigger!
overrides.reason: Guinea pig ~1 kg vs capybara ~50 kg; 100x is inflated.

overrides.find: Capybaras eat their own poop to get extra vitamins from their food.
overrides.replace: Capybaras eat some of their own soft droppings, which gives their tummies a second chance to get vitamins from their food.
overrides.reason: Accurate (cecotrophy) but blunt for a 3-8 read-aloud; clearer, gentler wording. Drop if the team prefers the gross-out hook.

overrides.find: Most of its kind live in just one special lake in Mexico.
overrides.replace: In the wild, it lives only in a few waterways near Mexico City.
overrides.reason: Wild axolotls survive only in the Xochimilco canals/lake remnants (Lake Chalco is gone); 'most live in one lake' misleads since many now live in captivity.

overrides.find: Hiding among the water plants, it lives in just one special lake in Mexico.
overrides.replace: Hiding among the water plants, it lives in the wild only near Mexico City, in Mexico.
overrides.reason: Same: wild range is the Xochimilco canals, not a single lake.

overrides.find: it can grow a perfect new one.
overrides.replace: it can grow a new one.
overrides.reason: Regeneration is remarkable but not always 'perfect'; hedge.

overrides.find: They can smell a single drop of blood from far away — like finding one red marble in a swimming pool full of clear ones.
overrides.replace: They have a super sense of smell and can notice tiny amounts of blood or fish scent in the water from far away.
overrides.reason: Single-drop-from-far-away is a popular myth; they detect very dilute scents (roughly parts per million) but not that extreme. Blood framing also unneeded for ages 3-8.

overrides.find: They can swim up to 56 kilometres per hour when they're chasing prey.
overrides.replace: They are fast swimmers and can zoom in short bursts of speed when they're chasing prey.
overrides.reason: 56 km/h is an inflated, poorly supported burst figure; ~40 km/h is the more defensible upper range. Dropping the number avoids a doubtful claim.

overrides.find: Great white sharks can grow as long as a minibus!
overrides.replace: The biggest great white sharks can grow as long as a minibus!
overrides.reason: Only the largest females reach ~6 m; also conflicts with the 16 ft typical size shown later.

overrides.find: The Amur tiger is the biggest cat in the whole world
overrides.replace: The Amur tiger is one of the biggest cats in the whole world
overrides.reason: Amur (Siberian) and Bengal tigers are comparable in size; 'the biggest' is unhedged.

overrides.find: other elephants feel the vibrations through their feet from kilometres away.
overrides.replace: other elephants can feel the vibrations through their feet from far away.
overrides.reason: Ground-borne reception over 'kilometres' is not firmly established at that range; hedge.

overrides.find: A baby elephant can stand up and walk just 20 minutes after being born.
overrides.replace: A baby elephant can stand up and walk within about half an hour of being born.
overrides.reason: Typically ~20-30+ minutes; avoid a too-precise figure.

overrides.find: They weigh about as much as a school bus full of kids
overrides.replace: They weigh about as much as a small school bus
overrides.reason: A bus full of kids is far heavier than 11,000 lb (about 5 tonnes); comparison is inflated.

overrides.find: African grasslands, savannas, and forests
overrides.replace: African grasslands, savannas, and forests
overrides.reason: Proper noun capitalization.

overrides.find: water colder than your freezer
overrides.replace: icy cold water
overrides.reason: Factual error: Antarctic seawater is about -2 C; a home freezer is about -18 C.

overrides.find: taller than most grown-ups
overrides.replace: about as tall as a grown-up
overrides.reason: 5 ft 7 in is average adult height, so 'taller than most grown-ups' contradicts the figure.

overrides.find: not because they're angry!
overrides.replace: it can be a way to show how big and strong they are!
overrides.reason: Chest-beating is a display that can also signal alarm or excitement; 'not angry' is an unhedged overclaim.

overrides.find: when they turn 12 years old
overrides.replace: when they are about 12 years old
overrides.reason: Age varies (roughly 12-13); hedge.

overrides.find: Created by Sea Shepherd in 2022, marking the 2021 Faroe Islands killing of 1,428 white-sided dolphins.
overrides.replace: Created by the conservation group Sea Shepherd in 2022 to raise awareness of the threats dolphins face.
overrides.reason: Origin is accurate but the graphic killing detail is unsuitable for a 3-8 read-aloud page.

overrides.find: Started by Earth Island Institute in 1990 during its campaign against dolphin deaths in tuna fishing.
overrides.replace: Started by Earth Island Institute in 1990 as part of its dolphin-safe tuna campaign.
overrides.reason: Softer wording for young listeners.

overrides.find: Dolphins leap out of the water to save energy when swimming fast.
overrides.replace: Dolphins often leap out of the water when swimming fast, which may help them save energy.
overrides.reason: Energy-saving is a hypothesis (porpoising), not settled fact; unhedged.

overrides.find: for up to three years
overrides.replace: for several years
overrides.reason: Bottlenose calves often stay with mothers 3-6 years; 'up to three' understates.

overrides.find: 8 out of every 10 times
overrides.replace: most of the time, often around 8 out of every 10 times
overrides.reason: Success rates vary by study (about 60-80%); hedge.

overrides.find: up to 60 kilometres per hour
overrides.replace: about 60 kilometres per hour
overrides.reason: Commonly cited top speed is ~60-70 km/h; 'up to' fine but avoid implying a cap.

overrides.find: Nepal, China, and Myanmar
overrides.replace: the Himalayan region, including Nepal, India, Bhutan, China, and Myanmar
overrides.reason: Incomplete range list; India and Bhutan are core range countries.

overrides.find: The 2026 dates are computed from the rule.
overrides.replace: It is held for a week in November; the exact dates change each year.
overrides.reason: Doubtful 'Nov 8' single-date claim; the event is a week whose dates vary (e.g. Nov 10-16 in 2019), and 'computed from the rule' is unverified.

overrides.find: they rarely come down to the ground
overrides.replace: they mostly stay up in the trees, though some Bornean orangutans do walk on the ground
overrides.reason: Bornean orangutans, especially males, travel on the ground more than Sumatran ones; hedge.

overrides.find: popularized from 1972
overrides.replace: and is said to have become popular from the 1970s
overrides.reason: Origin attribution is commonly repeated but weakly documented; hedge.

overrides.find: central and western Africa
overrides.replace: Africa
overrides.reason: Chimps also live in East Africa (e.g. Gombe, Tanzania, which the Chimpanzee Day origin line cites); central and western only is incomplete.

overrides.find: A single bite delivers enough venom to bring down 20 people — or one elephant.
overrides.replace: Its venom is very strong, so king cobras are best admired from far away.
overrides.reason: Frightening for 3-8 read-aloud and the 20-people/elephant claim is a repeated, loosely sourced figure.

overrides.find: almost 15 feet from head to tail
overrides.replace: up to about 15 feet or more from head to tail
overrides.reason: Typical adults are 10-13 ft, max about 18 ft; 'almost 15' as a typical figure is slightly off.

overrides.find: make a scary screeching sound instead
overrides.replace: make a raspy screech instead
overrides.reason: 'Scary' is unsuitable for young read-aloud and frames a natural call as frightening.

overrides.find: almost all the way around
overrides.replace: far around, about three-quarters of a circle,
overrides.reason: Owls rotate about 270 degrees, not nearly 360; 'almost all the way around' overstates.

overrides.find: They mate for life
overrides.replace: They often stay with the same partner for life
overrides.reason: Unhedged; barn owls are typically but not always monogamous.

overrides.find: They are the only wolves in the world that are not threatened by humans because almost no people live where they do.
overrides.replace: Very few people live where they do, so they almost never meet people.
overrides.reason: Unsupported absolute claim; Arctic wolves are not entirely free of human pressures (hunting, climate change).

overrides.find: Their front paws become five times more sensitive when wet, so they dip food in water to feel it better
overrides.replace: Their front paws feel even more when they are wet, so they dip food in water to feel it better
overrides.reason: Unsupported 'five times' figure.

overrides.find: Raccoons have super-sensitive fingers with more touch receptors than most animals.
overrides.replace: Raccoons have super-sensitive fingers with lots of touch receptors.
overrides.reason: Unhedged comparative claim.

overrides.find: They are excellent swimmers and can stay in water for several hours.
overrides.replace: They can swim well when they need to.
overrides.reason: Overstated swimming ability (the 'excellent swimmer' myth); duration claim unsupported.

overrides.find: They can leap across gaps as wide as a school bus is long without falling.
overrides.replace: They can leap across very wide gaps between trees.
overrides.reason: Gibbon leaps are roughly 8-10 m typically; a bus-length figure is inflated and invites a risky comparison.

overrides.find: they can zoom along faster than you can run
overrides.replace: they can zoom along very fast
overrides.reason: Hedge speed claim.

overrides.find: First held on Nov 7, 2015 by Project Numbat Inc., a volunteer group in Western Australia.
overrides.replace: First held on Nov 7, 2015 by Project Numbat Inc., a volunteer group in Western Australia; now held on the first Saturday of November.
overrides.reason: Verified first date; day now floats to first Saturday of November (Nov 7 is correct for 2026).

overrides.find: Horses were first tamed on the grasslands of Central Asia about six thousand years ago.
overrides.replace: Horses were first tamed on the grasslands of Eurasia about five thousand years ago.
overrides.reason: Genetic work places modern domestic horse lineage in the Pontic-Caspian steppe roughly 4,200 years ago, with earlier Botai horse use about 5,500 years ago; six thousand and Central Asia are overstated.

overrides.find: A baby horse can stand up and walk just one hour after being born.
overrides.replace: A baby horse can stand up and walk within a couple of hours after being born.
overrides.reason: Foals usually stand within about an hour or two; hedge.

overrides.find: Created by US Senate Resolution 452 in 2004
overrides.replace: Recognized by US Senate Resolution 452 in 2004
overrides.reason: A simple resolution recognizes/designates but does not create a law-based holiday.

overrides.find: They can jump farther than any other cat — up to 12 metres in one leap, which is longer than a school bus!
overrides.replace: They are amazing jumpers — one leap can cover about 40 feet, about as long as a school bus!
overrides.reason: 'Farther than any other cat' is unsupported; also metric units mixed into en-US feet/pounds copy.

overrides.find: A cougar can run as fast as a car in a school zone — up to 80 kilometres per hour for short distances.
overrides.replace: A cougar can run as fast as a car in a neighborhood — about 40 miles per hour for short distances.
overrides.reason: 80 km/h (50 mph) is an inflated figure; measured sprints are lower. Also fix mixed units for en-US.

overrides.find: Cougars have the longest back legs compared to their front legs of any cat, which helps them jump so far.
overrides.replace: Cougars have very long back legs compared to their front legs, which helps them jump so far.
overrides.reason: Superlative unhedged.

overrides.find: it's bright yellow and smaller than a bottle cap.
overrides.replace: it's bright yellow and small enough to sit in your hand.
overrides.reason: Golden poison frogs reach about 5 cm, larger than a bottle cap; also 'most poisonous' is better stated as one of the most poisonous.

overrides.find: The golden poison dart frog is the most poisonous
overrides.replace: The golden poison dart frog is one of the most poisonous animals in the world
overrides.reason: Hedge superlative.

overrides.find: Indigenous people in Colombia used the frogs' poison on their hunting arrows.
overrides.replace: Some Indigenous hunters in Colombia long ago used poison from a few kinds of these frogs on their hunting darts.
overrides.reason: Only a few species were used; avoid generalizing.

overrides.find: They weigh less than a single coin — you'd need hundreds to fill a teaspoon.
overrides.replace: They weigh about as much as a paperclip or two.
overrides.reason: Frogs weigh roughly 1-2 g each, so a teaspoon would hold only a handful; 'hundreds' is wrong.

overrides.find: across North America and parts of Asia
overrides.replace: across western North America
overrides.reason: Grizzlies are a North American brown bear; Asian brown bears are not called grizzlies.

overrides.find: They can smell food from 30 kilometres away — their nose is seven times stronger than a bloodhound's!
overrides.replace: They can smell food from a very long way away — their nose is much better than a dog's!
overrides.reason: 30 km and 7x bloodhound are shaky, unhedged figures.

overrides.find: A grizzly's bite is strong enough to crush a bowling ball.
overrides.reason: Dubious viral claim and a bit scary for a 3-8 read-aloud.

overrides.find: They have excellent night vision and can see in almost total darkness
overrides.replace: They have very good night vision and can see well in dim light
overrides.reason: No animal sees in near-total darkness; overstated.

overrides.find: that's as tall as a giraffe!
overrides.replace: that's taller than a door!
overrides.reason: 3 m is well short of a giraffe (4.5-5.5 m).

overrides.find: Leopards are the strongest climbers of all the big cats.
overrides.replace: Leopards are superb climbers, and often rest up in trees.
overrides.reason: Unhedged superlative.

overrides.find: who sneak up on their prey without making a sound
overrides.replace: who sneak up on their prey very quietly
overrides.reason: Absolute claim; leopards do make sounds.

overrides.find: can remember other donkeys and places for over 25 years
overrides.replace: can remember other donkeys and places for many years
overrides.reason: Specific 25-year figure is a single-source claim; hedge.

overrides.find: Turtles can't stick their heads out of their shells if the shell is too small — the shell grows with them!
overrides.replace: A turtle's shell is part of its body and grows with it — a turtle can't climb out of its shell!
overrides.reason: Original is garbled and factually wrong.

overrides.find: Some turtles can breathe through their butts!
overrides.replace: Some turtles can even take in a little oxygen through their back ends!
overrides.reason: Hedged to 'some' (certain freshwater species) and reworded kid-friendly.

overrides.find: because they have two voice boxes instead of one
overrides.replace: because they have a special voice box called a syrinx and a clever tongue
overrides.reason: 'Two voice boxes' is a myth; birds have one syrinx with two sides.

overrides.find: They have the strongest bite of any animal on Earth
overrides.replace: They have one of the strongest bites of any animal on Earth
overrides.reason: Unhedged superlative; only the saltwater crocodile holds the measured record, and this entry is a generic crocodile.

overrides.find: They can live for 70 to 100 years — longer than most humans!
overrides.replace: Some can live for 70 years or more!
overrides.reason: 100 years is inflated and unverified. 70+ is a hedged figure for the largest species.

overrides.find: they can stretch as wide as a small aeroplane!
overrides.replace: they can stretch wider than a grown-up's outstretched arms, about as wide as a car is long!
overrides.reason: A wingspan of about 11 ft (3.4 m) is nowhere near a small aeroplane (about 30 ft or more). The comparison is inflated.

overrides.find: They can smell food from over 20 kilometres away.
overrides.replace: They have a great sense of smell and can sniff out food from far away.
overrides.reason: The 20 km figure is a doubtful, unhedged claim. The documented behaviour is smelling food from long distances.

overrides.find: A bald eagle's grip is ten times stronger than a human's hand.
overrides.replace: A bald eagle's grip is much stronger than a human's hand.
overrides.reason: The exact 10x figure is a popular but loosely sourced number. A hedged version is safer.

iucnText.african_elephant: Endangered (savanna elephant) and Critically Endangered (forest elephant)
